title: constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured
owner: CC owns the code and the proofs. Akien owns the bound already given and not CC's to widen: orient, then constrain, then survey, and the other four wait on these three WORKING (ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap).
intention: constrain's floor AUTHORS the packet fields that are lookup rather than language — constraints and unknowns — and provenance for them stops being declared by the author and becomes DERIVED from whether the ceiling changed the floor's answer. The enabling primitive, missing until now, is address.component_of: given a PATH, which component owns it.
why:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, and the measurement is of the floor's input rather than its output, which is why it went unseen. constrain's floor tested each of orient's refs for membership in the component ROSTER — a set of bare NAMES. Since orient's floor started grounding its refs the same morning, a ref is a path far more often than a name: 266 of the 310 refs across the 45 berthed orient packets are paths. So the floor DISCARDED 86% of its own input and emitted an empty constraint list. An empty list is a legal list, so nothing redded anywhere in the system.

The consequence is the same shape orient's build closed one rung up, and it lands on the same instrument: 24 of 41 berthed constrain packets declare constraints: floor while the floor produced ZERO charter constraints for that input, and ten more produced exactly one, against ceiling lists running 5 to 19 items across five kinds. The number is a self-report.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM, and it is Akien's: he is deciding what to build next off skills/chart/dial.py. A pass that reports itself compiled when it is producing nothing tells him the cheapest remaining work is elsewhere, and the staircase stalls on a number nobody computed. Under the ruling of the same day the stakes are larger than tidiness — the ceiling for these passes is becoming Hex, and a failover only means anything if the floor's answer is a FACT the next rung can read.
traces_to: Ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap — the build order is Akien's: 'starting with orientation, we build out everything we can now ... orientation will add a json packet to the ticket, constrain will add to that. those can be completely deterministic. and ONCE THEY WORK we can start working on the other ones later.'
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. A provenance the author stamps is an unmeasured claim wearing a measurement's name.

Law 4 — a rule enforced by physics, not policy. 'Label the field honestly' is discipline; deriving the label removes the discretion, and constrain's charter gains gated_by: ['CC'] for the same reason orient's did.
Law 9 — red is the default, green is earned. 24 packets reading 'floor' for a field the floor never filled is a green the corpus never earned.

Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel. A ref that is a path had a settled answer available (component_dir's own AmbiguousComponent text already promises 'a path resolves unambiguously') and no implementation behind it, so every caller re-derived it or, here, silently gave up.

falsifier.proves_green: THREE PIECES, AND THE THIRD IS WHAT KEEPS THE FIRST TWO HONEST. (1) address.component_of resolves a PATH to its owning component — the other half of component_dir, asking the same question from the other end. THE DEEPEST ANCESTOR WINS, and that is the answer rather than a tie-break: components nest, so a file under devices/holder/machines/nested belongs to nested and holder is merely its holder. (2) floor_packet(intent_ref, root) authors constraints (every grounded component's falsifier, gates and owner, verbatim, each carrying its charter path and the field it came from) and unknowns (every ref it could NOT ground, carrying the why — 'not a component' is four distinct findings and they are told apart). bounds is NOT a candidate and never will be: what is in scope is a judgement about intent and no lookup produces it. (3) PROVENANCE FOR THOSE TWO IS DERIVED AT validate_constrain by re-running the floor over the packet's own intent_ref and comparing; a caller-supplied label that DISAGREES is refused rather than corrected. It sits at the gate because both doors a packet can leave by — the berth and the deposit — run that function.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) a packet is berthed whose provenance for constraints/unknowns was written by its sender rather than derived — the self-report restored; (2) THE DERIVED FLOOR FRACTION GOES UP WHILE THE PACKETS GET THINNER, i.e. the ceiling stopped writing its own law, ruling, ticket and memory constraints because the floor had already filled the field. This is the failure where every instrument in the system reads the damage as progress, and it is what the WATCHME exists for; (3) a floor-authored constraint names a source that does not exist on disk, or one the installed constraint_traces judge cannot resolve — a floor that invents is worse than a ceiling that invents, because it wears a measurement's provenance; (4) the 'floor' label becomes STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE for constraints — a label that can only ever take one value is a constant, not a measurement, and it blinds the dial to the thing the dial exists to see; (5) constrain grows a second opinion about where a ref points, in particular by teaching another component's judge a source spelling this module invented; (6) the change lands and the dial's readings for constrain and orient are left looking comparable when the two are now produced by different rules; (7) an oracle is consulted anywhere on this path, at fire time or at sleep — bin/cmd/determinism must keep reading this component PURE DETERMINISTIC and REFUSES GATE.
falsifier.horizon: Now, and it is done. Second rung of the build order Akien named on 2026-08-14; survey is next and inherits both halves, though NOT the survival rule — see the distinction below, because a rule copied forward without its reason is exactly how 'a tool holds no state' reached eight charters.

questions.a: THE SURVIVAL RULE DIVERGES FROM ORIENT'S DELIBERATELY, AND MIRRORING WOULD HAVE SHIPPED A CONSTANT. orient compares floor to ceiling by SET EQUALITY, which is right there because refs is a complete lookup result. constraints is not that shape: it is multi-source by construction — 148 charter, 110 ticket, 63 law, 33 ruling, 14 memory over 394 live items — and the floor owns exactly one kind. I built equality first, mirroring orient, and MEASURED 39 of 39 candidate packets reading 'claude' with no reachable path to anything else. The rule became two-sided: the floor's items survive unchanged AND no other charter-kind constraint appears beside them. Survival alone catches a DROPPED constraint and not a FORGED one, which is why both clauses are load-bearing.

'NOT A COMPONENT' WAS FOUR FINDINGS WEARING ONE SENTENCE, and they are now told apart in unknowns: an ambiguous NAME (two components share it, so the roster cannot answer); a roster/lookup disagreement (the roster says yes and resolution says no, which is a defect in the corpus rather than in the ref); a string naming neither a component nor a path that exists on disk (a stale pointer); and a real path that sits under NO component, so no charter bounds it (commons files, skills, top-level scripts). The first two are red, the last two are ordinary. Collapsing them hands a reader a sentence instead of a diagnosis.

THE 24 EMPTY-FLOOR PACKETS ARE HONEST AND THE BUILD SAYS SO. Their refs name paths retired by the 2026-08-13 rung move (115 of them) or commons and skill files under no component (47). That is the world having moved, not the floor failing, and it is recorded here so a later reader does not re-diagnose it.

THE DUPLICATE THAT WAS INVISIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION. Once path refs resolved, a component named BOTH by name and by path in the same orient packet produced every one of its constraints twice. It could not have been seen before, because a discarded ref cannot collide — and it could not be seen by reading the output either, since the duplicate texts are identical and read as a longer list of correct answers. A count tooth caught it; inspection would not have.

A PROOF CAN BE GREEN ABOUT A WORLD THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. constrain's fixture still built the flat cairn/<name>/ house that the rung move retired on 2026-08-13, and nothing redded because the component walk still finds a non-rung directory at top level. With every fixture component one level down, the deepest-owner rule had nothing to be wrong about — the fixture was testing an easier world than the real one.

THE SOURCE SPELLING WAS MINE TO FIX AND THE JUDGE WAS NOT. The floor first packed <path>#<field> into a constraint's source, and the installed judge refused all six, because it resolves a source through the one ref-resolution semantics the berth gate uses. The field moved to its own key rather than teaching that judge about fragments — a second spelling of 'where does this point' in a component this module is forbidden to shape (Law 6).

THIS TICKET IS STUCK AT TICKETME AND THE CODE IS DONE, PROVEN AND SEALED — RECORDED RATHER THAN ROUTED AROUND. The BUILDME crossing was refused by its own entry gate on 2026-08-14, verbatim: 'no berthed chart chain claims ticket constrain-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured — the build has no charted course'. THE GATE IS RIGHT. I built first and cast the ticket afterwards, so the preamble the chain exists to compile was never compiled and the build did not run inside it. The available fix is to run /chart now, and it is PLASTER: berths written after the build satisfy the check without establishing the thing it checks for, which is the hollow pass Law 8 exists to refuse. So the boat stays at TICKETME until the order is right, and the disposition is forward rather than retroactive — SURVEY IS CHARTED BEFORE IT IS BUILT. That also settles what the chain runs on: charting survey's own build fires stage 2, which is constrain, and berths the first post-door constrain packets the WATCHME above is waiting for.

ORIENT REACHED PROVED ONLY BECAUSE ITS TICKET FILE WAS AUTHORED PAST THIS GATE, and that is the same defect one rung up rather than a precedent. MEASURED across the 41 tickets ever cast through /sorted: 40 carry an intent_berth and orient's is the only one that carries none, and git shows its file was first committed with its cursor already at [BUILDME] — a position no crossing ever moved it to, because the /sorted door refuses a cast cursor past TICKETME and the ticket FILE has no door at all. So the entry gate never fired on it. This is the casting-has-no-chokepoint IOU already named in cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py, with its n=2 now measured rather than predicted; the seven other tickets born past TICKETME all carry an intent_berth, so the corpus is not generally leaking — these two builds are.

COMPONENT_OF BELONGS IN base AND NOT IN constrain, and the reason is not tidiness. It is the other half of a question the corpus already asks in two places and answers in one; AmbiguousComponent's error text has been promising the behaviour to readers who had no way to get it. Written with Path.expanduser so cairn/tools/base keeps importing pathlib and nothing else — a property constrain's own import site measures and leans on, which a convenience import would have quietly cost.

watchme.trigger: each read of the probe over ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets — no clock and no new firing path; it rides the shim's existing pulse and the read-side overdue() door, the same seam every other probe in the corpus sits on. TRUE when at least 12 packets have berthed UNDER THE NEW DOOR (filename stamp >= 20260814T000000) AND their median non-charter constraint count has fallen BELOW the minimum of the closed pre-build corpus, which is 2 — no packet the ceiling ever wrote carried fewer than two constraints of its own. The threshold is recomputed from that corpus on every read rather than frozen as a literal, so it is the corpus's number and not a constant someone chose (a hand-set gate is a learned value stranded in a human's head).
watchme.enough: CLEARED when at least 12 post-door packets have berthed AND their median non-charter count is holding at or above that pre-build floor — the claim this build has to survive. Deliberately NOT cleared on 'the floor earned its label': a rising floor fraction is what crowding-out LOOKS like, so clearing on it would retire the watch at exactly the moment it should bite. Measured rather than asserted — a starved fixture and a healthy fixture both read earned_floor 14 of 14, so the label cannot distinguish them and this clause must not rest on it.
watchme.carrier: cairn/devices/builder/machines/constrain/probes/crowding_out.py — module-level PROBE carrying both populations in ONE report (pre-build n, median, min; post-build n, median, min; the charter total; the per-field floor tally; and the starved berths by name), because a failure report delivers everything needed to resolve it on the first pass.
watchme.nexus: hypothesize — the finding is 'the ceiling stopped writing its own constraints', which is a hypothesis about why and not a fact about what: the floor's bulk is one cause and a ceiling gone quiet for unrelated reasons is another, and the report carries the charter-per-berth ratio that tells them apart.
watchme.consumer: harbor_master. It deposits and pokes and carries no authority: the back-edge that re-opens this ticket is the owner's act (Law 6). A fire means read skills/chart/SKILL.md stage 2 first — the ceiling is instructed to carry the floor's constraints through and ADD the kinds that need judgement, and a thin packet usually means that instruction now reads as 'the list is already full'.

intent_berth: none, because the intention is not mine and did not need the cheapest gate to survive: it is Akien's ruled build order of 2026-08-14 (ruling 2026-08-14-the-preamble-compiles-to-learn-not-to-be-cheap, 'starting with orientation, we build out everything we can now ... constrain will add to that'), whose sibling rung orient is CairnCommons/tickets/orient-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured.json. /intent exists to kill an intention that should not exist before cost is spent on it; an intention handed down by the owner with its sequencing already fixed has had that question answered by the hand that outranks the gate. RECORDED RATHER THAN FIRED, which is the legal answer the entry gate itself names — and it is the honest one only because the referents above resolve. Contrast the chart lack below, which has NO honest post-hoc answer and is therefore not exempted.
chart_claim: validate-20260828T052319-67401a3d141c — chart chain filled 2026-08-28 with real content; verdict berthed at verdict-20260828T052351-1ecf29b8eaf0
dependencies: MEASURED, not assumed: floor_facts already computes the component roster and path existence, and the constraint_traces judge already resolves a constraint's source through the berth gate's own ref semantics. Both applied unchanged.

orient-floor-authors-and-provenance-is-measured is the parent pattern and had to land first — constrain's floor reads the orient packet, so a floor that authors here needs refs that are grounded there. It PROVED the same morning.
NOT a dependency: hex.local. This build is what gives Hex something to fail over FROM, and it needs nothing from the box.
NOT a dependency and checked before building: no change to skills/chart/dial.py, whose code is faithful — what changes is that the labels it reads become derived.

chart_notes.orient: The code is at cairn/devices/builder/machines/constrain/constrain.py: _resolve_ref handles both ref shapes and names the four failure reasons, _charter_constraints emits one constraint per bounding field, floor_packet authors, FLOOR_AUTHORED names the two, _survived is the two-sided rule, measured_provenance re-runs the floor, refuse_misdeclared_floor_provenance is the refusal, and validate_constrain is the gate both doors run. The new primitive is component_of in cairn/tools/base/address.py, beside component_dir. Proofs: 16 teeth at the machine, one at address's own proof for the deepest-owner rule. The reading instrument is skills/chart/dial.py. The evidence is 41 berthed constrain packets and 45 orient packets under ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/.
chart_notes.constrain: IN: constrain, component_of, their proofs, constrain's charter, one probe. OUT and stated: survey and the five nexi after it (Akien's order is one at a time, ONCE THEY WORK); the dial's own code; anything on hex.local; the six remaining charters of a-charter-may-not-assert-a-file-that-is-not-there; and any widening of what the floor authors — bounds stays the ceiling's forever.
chart_notes.validate: The tooth a hollow build fails runs in TWO directions, and the second is the one mirroring orient would have missed. FORWARD: berth a packet declaring constraints: floor for a list the floor did not produce, and require refusal — a hollow build accepts the sender's dict, which is today's 24 packets. BACKWARD: take a packet the floor's answer genuinely survived into and require the label to read 'floor'. A build whose rule is set equality passes the first and fails the second while looking correct, because 'nothing ever earns it' and 'nothing ever forges it' are the same observation from one side. Run by hand against the live rule: honest -> floor 17/17, drop a floor constraint -> claude 17/17, forge a charter-kind one -> claude 17/17, add a ticket-kind one -> still floor.

filed_edges: THE DIAL NOW READS TWO DIFFERENT RULES AS ONE NUMBER. orient's _survived is set equality and constrain's is two-sided survival, both spelled 'floor'. Nothing announces the difference, and a reader comparing the two nexi is comparing two measurements. Either the dial grows a way to say which rule produced a reading, or the difference is footnoted where a reader will actually meet it. Not built here — it is the dial's own component and this ticket does not touch it.

THE THIRD OUTCOME orient's ticket already filed has its first real instance here: the ceiling EXTENDS the floor's answer (adds a ticket-kind or law-kind constraint beside the floor's charter ones) and that correctly reads 'floor' under the two-sided rule — but the ceiling adding a legitimate CHARTER-kind constraint the floor could not reach reads 'claude' and loses the fact that the floor's part survived. Measurable once post-door packets exist; not invented before then.

206 of the 246 non-charter live constraints are kinds the floor structurally cannot produce, and a further 20 one-off kinds appear exactly once or twice each (decision, proof, code-precedent, store-charter, prior-art, trouble...). That long tail is either a vocabulary that wants settling or evidence that constraint kinds are correctly open. Not a defect and not resolved — recorded so the question is asked from data when it is asked.

The floor reaches a component's charter and stops there. A constraint could equally be read from a ticket's own falsifier or from a law, both of which are lookups over files on disk. Deliberately out of this build (build minimal, grow against need), and it is the obvious next place the floor could compile into — but only against evidence that the ceiling is spending its judgement transcribing them.
